subject: Hospitality
title: Marriott's Adoption in the 1980s
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Marriott's Adoption in the 1980s.

hook.text: Marriott was the first hotel chain to apply airline-style yield management. It changed how the entire industry prices rooms.

buildup.text: In the mid-1980s, Marriott hired analysts who studied demand patterns to set different rates for different days and segments.

discovery.text: The system identified that business travelers book late and pay more, while leisure travelers book early and seek deals.

twist.text: Marriott's revenue management added $100 million in annual revenue without adding a single new room.

climax.text: Every major hotel chain followed. Revenue management became a mandatory discipline, not just an experiment.

punchline.text: Same rooms, different prices, $100 million more. Math transformed hospitality.

quiz.question: How did Marriott's revenue management add $100 million without new rooms?
options: Smarter pricing based on demand patterns and guest segments
